cohort: The study included 25 anemic women who underwent cesarean delivery and received at least one blood transfusion.
finding: The analysis demonstrated that a 1-point increase in preoperative hemoglobin could have prevented transfusions in 92% of cases, and a hemoglobin of 10 g/dL could have prevented transfusions in 96% of cases, highlighting the potential to avoid transfusions with modest Hb increases.
mod_finding: The study specifically focused on cesarean deliveries, demonstrating that improved preoperative hemoglobin levels could reduce transfusion needs during this mode of birth.
